You are using the CSES Standards Wiki. CSES refers to the Comparative Study of
Electoral Systems project and its Secretariat knowledge base. The source corpus is
`knowledge_base_final/`, containing 215 Markdown source documents and about
789,912 words after prior consolidation.

This `cses_wiki/` folder is the token-efficient working layer. Load this file
and `ROUTER.md` first. Then open the most relevant topic or procedure page. Only
open original source documents when the answer needs exact wording, provenance,
dates, or policy authority.

Main knowledge domains include: Training, Operations, Demographic Coding, Documentation Standards, Data Protection, Education Coding, District Data, Macro Data.

Answering rules:

- Prefer current procedure pages over raw historical source documents.
- Cite source paths when answering procedural, policy, legal/privacy, or
  documentation-standard questions.
- Distinguish current operational guidance from historical meeting, agenda, or
  training material.
- If a source is old but still kept as reference material, say so instead of
  presenting it as automatically current.
- For data-protection or legal/privacy questions, provide source-backed operational
  guidance and flag that institutional review may be needed for final decisions.
- When project calendars, release dates, or current staff assignments matter, verify
  against current project records outside this generated standards wiki.
